schema.description: Region ID.
Instance ID.

Username.

- You can use an asterisk (\*) to represent all usernames.

> * Only after authorization is granted to all users can you query the authorized users using an asterisk (\*).

Resource type. Valid values:

- **Topic**: message topic.

- **Group**: consumer group.

- **Cluster**: instance.

- **TransactionalId**: transaction ID.

Resource name.

- The name of the resource, which can be a topic name, Group ID, cluster name, or transaction ID.

- You can use an asterisk (\*) to represent all resources of this type.

> * Only after authorization is granted to all resources can you query the authorized resources using an asterisk (\*).

Matching pattern. Valid values:

- **LITERAL**: exact match

- **PREFIXED**: prefix match

Operation type. Valid values:

- **Write**: write

- **Read**: read

- **Describe**: read TransactionalId

- **IdempotentWrite**: idempotent write to Cluster

- **IDEMPOTENT\_WRITE**: idempotent write to Cluster, only available for Serverless instances.

- **DESCRIBE\_CONFIGS**: query configuration, only available for Serverless instances.

Batch authorization operation types. Multiple operations are separated by commas (,).

Valid values:

- **Write**: read

- **Read**: write

- **Describe**: read TransactionalId

- **IdempotentWrite**: idempotent write to Cluster

- **IDEMPOTENT\_WRITE**: idempotent write to Cluster, only available for Serverless instances.

- **DESCRIBE\_CONFIGS**: query configuration, only available for Serverless instances.

> This parameter is only supported for Serverless instances.

Authorization method. Valid values:

- **DENY**: deny.

- **ALLOW**: allow.

> This parameter is only supported for Serverless instances.

Source IP.

> - Only specific IP addresses or \* (all IPs) are supported. IP address ranges are not supported.
>
> - This parameter is only supported for Serverless instances.

CreatePostPayInstance.summary: This operation creates a pay-as-you-go instance and returns the instance ID and order ID.

schema.description: The region ID of the instance.

The disk type. Valid values:

- **0**: ultra disk

- **1**: SSD

> This parameter is not required when you create a Serverless instance.

The disk capacity.

For more information about the value range, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required when you create a Serverless instance.

The deployment type. Valid values:

- **4**: instance that is accessible over the internet and a VPC

- **5**: instance that is accessible only over a VPC

The Internet traffic.

- This parameter is required if you set **DeployType** to **4**.

- For more information about the value range, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required when you create a Serverless instance.

The number of partitions.

- For more information about the value range, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required if the instance is a Serverless instance.

The billing method. Valid values:

- 1 (default): pay-as-you-go for reserved instances.

- 3: pay-as-you-go for reserved capacity and elastic scaling of Serverless instances.

The edition of the instance.

If you set the PaidType parameter to 1 (pay-as-you-go for reserved instances), valid values are:

- normal: Standard Edition (High-write)

- professional: Professional Edition (High-write)

- professionalForHighRead: Professional Edition (High-read)

If you set the PaidType parameter to 3 (pay-as-you-go for reserved capacity and elastic scaling of Serverless instances), valid values are:

- basic: Serverless Basic Edition

- normal: Serverless Standard Edition

- professional: Serverless Professional Edition

For more information about these instance editions, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The traffic specification.

- For more information about the value range, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required when you create a Serverless instance.

The ID of the resource group.

If you do not specify this parameter, the instance is added to the default resource group. You can view the resource group ID in the Resource Group console.
The tags.

Key.description:
The tag key of the resource.

- The value of N can be from 1 to 20.

- If this parameter is left empty, all tag keys are matched.

- The tag key can be up to 128 characters in length. It cannot start with aliyun or acs: and cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

Value.description:
The tag value of the resource.

- The value of N can be from 1 to 20.

- If the tag key is empty, this parameter must also be empty. If this parameter is empty, all tag values are matched.

- The tag value can be up to 128 characters in length. It cannot start with aliyun or acs: and cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

CreatePostPayInstance.title: CreatePostPayInstance

CreatePostPayOrder.summary: Pay-as-you-go instances are billed based on actual usage. This billing method is ideal for testing or short-term scenarios with unpredictable traffic peaks. This topic describes how to call the CreatePostPayOrder operation to create a pay-as-you-go instance.

schema.description: The region ID of the instance.

The disk type. Valid values:

- **0**: Ultra disk

- **1**: SSD

> Do not specify this parameter if you create a Serverless instance.

The disk capacity.

For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> Do not specify this parameter if you create a Serverless instance.

The deployment type. Valid values:

- **4**: An instance that is accessible from the Internet and a VPC.

- **5**: An instance that is accessible only from a VPC.

The Internet traffic.

- This parameter is required if you set **DeployType** to **4**.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> Do not specify this parameter if you create a Serverless instance.

The peak traffic. This parameter is not recommended.

- You must specify this parameter or \`IoMaxSpec\`. If you specify both parameters, the value of \`IoMaxSpec\` takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only \`IoMaxSpec\`.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> Do not specify this parameter if you create a Serverless instance.

The number of partitions. This parameter is recommended.

- You must specify this parameter or \`TopicQuota\`. We recommend that you specify only this parameter.

- If you specify both this parameter and \`TopicQuota\`, the system verifies whether the values of the two parameters are equivalent based on the previous topic-based sales model. If the values are not equivalent, the system returns a failure. If the values are equivalent, the purchase is made based on the number of partitions.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> Do not specify this parameter if you create a Serverless instance.

The number of topics. This parameter is not recommended.

- You must specify this parameter or \`PartitionNum\`. We recommend that you specify only \`PartitionNum\`.

- If you specify both this parameter and \`PartitionNum\`, the system verifies whether the values of the two parameters are equivalent based on the previous topic-based sales model. If the values are not equivalent, the system returns a failure. If the values are equivalent, the purchase is made based on the number of partitions.

- The default value of this parameter varies based on the traffic specification. You are charged for the extra topics that exceed the default value.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> Do not specify this parameter if you create a Serverless instance.

The billing method. Valid values:

- 1 (default): Pay-as-you-go for a reserved instance.

- 3: Pay-as-you-go for a reserved Serverless instance and pay-as-you-go for elastic scaling of a Serverless instance.

The specification type.

If you set \`PaidType\` to 1 (pay-as-you-go for a reserved instance), valid values are:

- normal: Standard Edition (High-write)

- professional: Professional Edition (High-write)

- professionalForHighRead: Professional Edition (High-read)

If you set \`PaidType\` to 3 (pay-as-you-go for a reserved Serverless instance and pay-as-you-go for elastic scaling of a Serverless instance), valid values are:

- basic: Serverless Basic Edition

- normal: Serverless Standard Edition

- professional: Serverless Professional Edition

For more information about these specification types, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The traffic specification. This parameter is recommended.

- You must specify this parameter or \`IoMax\`. If you specify both parameters, the value of this parameter takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only this parameter.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> Do not specify this parameter if you create a Serverless instance.

The ID of the resource group.

If you do not set this parameter, the instance is added to the default resource group. You can view the resource group ID in the Resource Group console.
The tags.

Key.description:
The tag key.

- N can be an integer from 1 to 20.

- If this parameter is empty, all tag keys are matched.

- The tag key can be up to 128 characters in length. It cannot start with \`aliyun\` or \`acs:\` and cannot contain \`http\://\` or \`https\://\`.

Value.description:
The tag value.

- N can be an integer from 1 to 20.

- This parameter must be empty if the tag key is empty. If this parameter is empty, all tag values are matched.

- The tag value can be up to 128 characters in length. It cannot start with \`aliyun\` or \`acs:\` and cannot contain \`http\://\` or \`https\://\`.

schema.description: The settings of the Serverless instance. This parameter is required if you create a Serverless instance.

ReservedPublishCapacity.description:
The reserved capacity for message publishing. You can specify only an integer for this parameter. The minimum value is 60. This parameter is required if you create a Serverless instance.

> The actual upper limit is subject to the inventory in the current region. For more information, see the instance purchase page.

ReservedSubscribeCapacity.description:
The reserved capacity for message subscription. You can specify only an integer for this parameter. The minimum value is 20. This parameter is required if you create a Serverless instance.

> The actual upper limit is subject to the inventory in the current region. For more information, see the instance purchase page.

Code.description: The return code. A value of 200 indicates success.

Success.description: Indicates whether the call was successful.

CreatePostPayOrder.description: Before you call this operation, make sure you understand the billing methods and pricing of pay-as-you-go instances. For more information, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

schema.description: The region ID of the instance.

The disk type. Valid values:

- **0**: ultra disk
- **1**: SSD

> This parameter is not required when you create a Confluent series instance.

The disk capacity. Unit: GB.

For the valid range, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required when you create a Confluent series instance.

The number of partitions to purchase.

- For the valid range, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required if the instance is a Confluent instance.

The deployment type. Valid values:

- **4**: Internet/VPC instance
- **5**: VPC instance

> If you create a Confluent series instance, you cannot select the deployment type. You can only set the value to 5. After the purchase, you can adjust whether each component is open to the Internet.

The Internet traffic.

- If **DeployType** is set to **4**, you must specify this parameter.
- For the valid range, see [pay-as-you-go](~~72142~~).

> This parameter is not required when you create a Confluent series instance.

The specification type.

Valid values for Kafka instances:

- **normal**: Standard Edition (high write)
- **professional**: Professional Edition (high write)
- **professionalForHighRead**: Professional Edition (high read)

Valid values for Confluent instances:

- **professional**: Professional Edition
- **enterprise**: Enterprise Edition

For more information, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The traffic specification.

- For the valid range, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required when you create a Confluent series instance.

The resource group ID.

If this parameter is not set, the instance is placed in the default resource group. You can view the resource group ID in the Resource Group console.
The list of tags.

Key.description:
The tag key of the resource.

- N ranges from 1 to 20.
- If this parameter is empty, all tag keys are matched.
- The tag key can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with aliyun or acs:. It cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

Value.description:
The tag value of the resource.

- N ranges from 1 to 20.
- This parameter can be empty.
- The tag value can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with aliyun or acs:. It cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

schema.description:

- **0**: subscription
- **4**: Confluent series subscription

CreatePrePayInstance.title: CreatePrePayInstance
CreatePrePayInstance.summary: Creates a subscription instance and returns the instance ID and order ID.

CreatePrePayOrder.summary: Subscription instances require prepayment for resources and are ideal for long-term, stable business scenarios. This topic describes how to call the CreatePrePayOrder operation to create a subscription instance.

schema.description: The region ID of the instance.

The disk type. Valid values:

- **0**: ultra disk

- **1**: SSD

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you do not need to pass this parameter.

The disk capacity. Unit: GB.

For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you do not need to pass this parameter.

The number of partitions (recommended).

- You must specify either the number of partitions or the topic specification. We recommend that you specify only the number of partitions.

- If you specify both the number of partitions and the topic specification, the system verifies whether the number of partitions is equivalent to the topic specification based on the old topic sales model. If they are not equivalent, the system returns a failure. If they are equivalent, the system makes the purchase based on the number of partitions.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you do not need to pass this parameter.

The number of topics (not recommended).

- You must specify either the number of partitions or the topic specification. We recommend that you specify only the number of partitions.

- If you specify both the number of partitions and the topic specification, the system verifies whether the number of partitions is equivalent to the topic specification based on the old topic sales model. If they are not equivalent, the system returns a failure. If they are equivalent, the system makes the purchase based on the number of partitions.

- The default value varies based on the traffic specification. Additional fees are charged if the value exceeds the default value.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you do not need to pass this parameter.

The deployment type. Valid values:

- **4**: Internet/VPC instance

- **5**: VPC instance

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you cannot select the deployment type. You can only set the value to 5. After the purchase, you can adjust whether each component is open to the Internet.

The Internet traffic.

- If **DeployType** is set to **4**, you must specify this parameter.

- For the valid values, see [pay-as-you-go](~~72142~~).

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you do not need to pass this parameter.

The specification type.

Valid values for Kafka instances:

- **normal**: Standard Edition (high write)

- **professional**: Professional Edition (high write)

- **professionalForHighRead**: Professional Edition (high read)

Valid values for Confluent instances:

- **professional**: Professional Edition

- **enterprise**: Enterprise Edition

For more information, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The traffic specification (recommended).

- You must specify either **IoMax** or **IoMaxSpec**. If you specify both parameters, **IoMaxSpec** takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only **IoMaxSpec**.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you do not need to pass this parameter.

The traffic peak (not recommended).

- You must specify either **IoMax** or **IoMaxSpec**. If you specify both parameters, **IoMaxSpec** takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only **IoMaxSpec**.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If you are creating a Confluent series instance, you do not need to pass this parameter.

The resource group ID.

If you do not specify this parameter, the instance is added to the default resource group. You can view the resource group ID in the Resource Group console.
The list of tags.

Key.description:
The tag key of the resource.

- N ranges from 1 to 20.

- If this parameter is empty, all tag keys are matched.

- The tag key can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with aliyun or acs:. It cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

Value.description:
The tag value of the resource.

- N ranges from 1 to 20.

- This parameter can be empty.

- The tag value can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with aliyun or acs:. It cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

schema.description:

- **0**: subscription

- **4**: Confluent series subscription

> This parameter is required when you create a Confluent series instance.

The SASL mechanism. Valid values:

- plain: a simple username and password authentication mechanism. Message Queue for Apache Kafka optimizes the PLAIN mechanism to support the dynamic creation of SASL users without the need to restart the instance.

- scram: a username and password authentication mechanism that provides higher security than the PLAIN mechanism. Message Queue for Apache Kafka uses Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM)-SHA-256.

- LDAP: This value is applicable only when you create users for Confluent instances.

Default value: plain.

- SCRAM-SHA-512 (default)

CreateScheduledScalingRule.title: CreateScheduledScalingRule
CreateScheduledScalingRule.description: ###### This operation supports only serverless instances.
CreateScheduledScalingRule.summary: After you deploy a serverless instance, you can use this API to create a scheduled scaling rule for the instance.

schema.description: The ID of the instance.

The name of the topic.

- Reserved instance: The name can contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, underscores (\_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). The name must be 3 to 64 characters in length.

- Serverless instance: The name can contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, underscores (\_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). The name must be 1 to 249 characters in length.

The remarks on the topic.

- The remarks can contain only letters, digits, underscores (\_), and hyphens (-).

- The remarks must be 3 to 64 characters in length.
The ID of the region where the instance that contains the topic is located.

The cleanup policy for the topic. This parameter is available only if the storage engine of the topic is local storage. Valid values:

- false: The delete cleanup policy.

- true: The compact cleanup policy.

The number of partitions in the topic.

- The value must be an integer from 1 to 360.

- The console suggests a number of partitions based on the instance type. Follow the suggestion to reduce the risk of data skew.

Default value:

- Reserved instance: 12

- Serverless instance: 3

The storage engine of the topic. Valid values:

- false: cloud storage.

- true: local storage.

The number of replicas for the topic.

- This parameter is available only if **LocalTopic** is set to **true**.

- The value must be an integer from 1 to 3.

> If you set the number of replicas to **1**, you may lose data. Set this parameter with caution.

The minimum number of in-sync replicas (ISRs).

- This parameter is available only if **LocalTopic** is set to **true**.

- The value of this parameter must be smaller than the number of replicas for the topic.

- The value must be an integer from 1 to 3.

The advanced configurations of the topic.

- Configure this parameter in the JSON format.

- This parameter is available only if **LocalTopic** is set to **true**.

- The following configurations are supported for reserved instances:

  - **retention.ms**: The message retention period. The value must be an integer from 3,600,000 to 31,536,000,000. Unit: milliseconds.

  - **max.message.bytes**: The maximum size of a message that can be sent. The value must be an integer from 1,048,576 to 10,485,760. Unit: bytes.

  - message.timestamp.type: The timestamp type of a message. Valid values: CreateTime or LogAppendTime. CreateTime indicates that the message timestamp is the time when the producer creates the message. If you do not specify a timestamp, the client time is used. LogAppendTime indicates that the message timestamp is the time when the server stores the message. The default value is CreateTime. We recommend that you set this parameter to **LogAppendTime**.

- The following configurations are supported for Serverless instances:

  - **retention.hours**: The message retention period. The value is of the string type. The value must be an integer from 24 to 8,760.

  - **max.message.bytes**: The maximum size of a message that can be sent. The value is of the string type. The value must be an integer from 1,048,576 to 10,485,760.

  - message.timestamp.type: The timestamp type of a message. Valid values: CreateTime or LogAppendTime. CreateTime indicates that the message timestamp is the time when the producer creates the message. If you do not specify a timestamp, the client time is used. LogAppendTime indicates that the message timestamp is the time when the server stores the message. The default value is CreateTime. We recommend that you set this parameter to **LogAppendTime**.
The list of tags.

Key.description:
The tag key of the resource.

- N specifies the number of the tag. The value of N must be an integer from 1 to 20.

- If this parameter is left empty, all tag keys are matched.

- The tag key can be up to 128 characters in length. It cannot start with `aliyun` or `acs:`, and cannot contain `http://` or `https://`.

Value.description:
The tag value of the resource.

- N specifies the number of the tag. The value of N must be an integer from 1 to 20.

- The tag value can be empty.

- The tag value can be up to 128 characters in length. It cannot start with aliyun or acs:, and cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

Instance ID.

- **plain**: A simple username and password verification mechanism. MSMQ optimizes the PLAIN mechanism to support adding SASL users dynamically without restarting the instance.

- **scram**: A username and password verification mechanism with higher security than PLAIN. MSMQ uses SCRAM-SHA-256.

- **LDAP**: Only applicable for deleting Confluent instance users.

Default value: **plain**.

Encryption method. Valid values:

- SCRAM-SHA-512 (selected by default)

- SCRAM-SHA-256

GetConsumerList.title: GetConsumerList

GetConsumerProgress.summary: Queries the consumption status of a consumer group.

schema.description: The instance ID.
The name of the consumer group.
The region ID of the instance.

Specifies whether to hide the \`LastTimestamp\` parameter. The default value is false. Set this parameter to true for better performance.

> - If you set this parameter to true, -1 is returned for the \`LastTimestamp\` parameter. Otherwise, a specific value is returned. This parameter is supported only for topics of cloud storage on provisioned instances.
>
> - This operation processes a large amount of data and consumes a high degree of performance. Set this parameter to true to reduce the processing time.

Code.description: The status code. A value of 200 indicates that the request is successful.

Success.description: Indicates whether the call is successful.

LastTimestamp.description:
The latest time when a message was stored. This time is calculated based on the consumer offsets of all topics in the consumer group.

> - This parameter is not supported for topics on Serverless instances or topics that use local storage on provisioned instances. In these cases, -1 is returned.
>
> - For topics that use cloud storage on provisioned instances, this parameter returns the message creation timestamp. This happens only after you submit the consumer offset for a consumer group that was created in the console or by an API call. If the message has no creation timestamp, -1 is returned.

TotalDiff.description: The total number of unconsumed messages in all topics. This value is the message accumulation.

state.description:
The status of the consumer group:

- UNKNOWN

- PREPARING\_REBALANCE

- COMPLETING\_REBALANCE

- STABLE

- DEAD

- EMPTY

TopicList.description: The list of consumption progress for each topic in the consumer group.

TotalDiff.description: The total number of unconsumed messages in the topic. This value is the message accumulation.

LastTimestamp.description:
The latest time when a message was stored. This time is calculated based on the consumer offsets of all topics to which the consumer group subscribes.

> - This parameter is not supported for topics on Serverless instances or topics that use local storage on provisioned instances. In these cases, -1 is returned.
>
> - For topics that use cloud storage on provisioned instances, this parameter returns the message creation timestamp. This happens only after you submit the consumer offset for a consumer group that was created in the console or by an API call. If the message has no creation timestamp, -1 is returned.

The time when the message at the consumer offset of the partition was stored.

The type of client IP query. You can choose from three methods.

- byInstance: Query client IPs for the instance within the specified time range.

- byTopic: Query client IPs for the topic within the specified time range.

- byGroup: Query client IPs for the group within the specified time range.

Success.description: Indicates whether the request was successful.

Code.description: Return code. A value of 200 indicates success.

SearchTimeRange.description:
The time range for querying client IPs.

> This range is 1 hour. If the start time and end time you enter exceed 1 hour, only data within 1 hour will be queried.

Num.description:
Statistics count.

> This represents the number of connections from the same IP with different ports that the server detected within your specified time range

Name.description:
Request name.

> This indicates what type of request the client sent to the server within the specified time range.

Alert.description:
If this value is true, it indicates that the minor version is not the latest version.

> If your server minor version is not the latest version, the sampling logs may not be accurate enough, resulting in less precise IP information statistics. Therefore, it is recommended that you upgrade the server minor version as soon as possible.

TimeLimitDay.description:

> This range is 7 days. If the start time and end time you enter exceed 7 days, only data within 7 days will be queried.

GetKafkaClientIp.title: GetKafkaClientIp
GetKafkaClientIp.summary: Retrieves the IP addresses of Kafka clients.
GetKafkaClientIp.description:
- The IP information is retrieved from the sampling logs of client requests to the server through the Kafka API.

- The count indicates the number of connections from a single IP address using different ports that the server detected within the specified time range.

- If your server is not running the latest minor version, the sampling logs may be inaccurate and provide less precise IP information. We recommend that you upgrade the server to the latest minor version.

GetRiskList.summary: Queries the list of threats on an instance.

schema.description: The region ID of the instance.
The ID of the instance.
The start index for paging.
The page size.

RiskList.description: The list of threat items for the instance.

CreateTime.description: The timestamp when the threat was created. Unit: milliseconds.

GradeType.description:
The metric rating. Valid values:

- A: Healthy.

- B: Suboptimal.

- F: Poor.

Health.description:
Indicates whether the instance is healthy.
This is a Boolean parameter. Valid values:

- true: The instance is healthy.

- false: The instance is unhealthy.

LastAlarmTime.description: The timestamp of the last alert. Unit: milliseconds.

LevelType.description:
The risk level. Valid values:

- 0: Urgent.

- 1: Important.

- 2: Normal.

ModifiedTime.description: The timestamp when the threat was last modified. Unit: milliseconds.

Name.description:
The name of the threat item.

> There are 24 types of names.
>
> - For more information, see the supplementary notes at the end of this document.

RelationList.description: A cascading structure. The system determines whether to nest another layer of report data based on the values of outer fields.

ReportTips.example: 相关问题里的Topic存在碎片化发送问题，请参考文档进行优化

ReportType.description:
The report type of the threat item. Valid values:

- topic: Optimization is required for a specific topic.

- group: Optimization is required for a specific group.

- doc: Optimization must be performed based on a document.

- commonBuy: An upgrade or a similar operation is required for the returned threat item.

- mdsKey: You only need to fix the threat based on the suggestions in ReportTips.

ReportValue.description:
The value of the report.

> - If ReportType is doc, ReportValue returns the document ID. You can construct the URL to the document by replacing the ${reportValue} variable in the following URL with the returned value: <props="china">https\://help.aliyun.com/document\_detail/${reportValue}.html</props><props="intl">https\://www\.alibabacloud.com/help/document\_detail/${reportValue}.html</props>
>
> - If ReportType is commonBuy, an upgrade or a similar operation is required.
>
> - If ReportType is topic, the value of ReportValue is the name of the topic that needs to be fixed.
>
> - If ReportType is group, the value of ReportValue is the name of the group that needs to be fixed.
>
> - If ReportType is mdsKey, you only need to fix the threat based on the suggestions in ReportTips.

Status.description:
The status of the threat item. This parameter indicates whether the threat has been fixed. Valid values:

- 0: To be fixed.

- -1: Ignored.

- 1: Fixed.

Type.description:
The type of the threat item.

> There are 24 types of threats.
>
> - For more information, see the supplementary notes at the end of this document.

Value.description:
The value calculated by the system.

> If ReportType is doc, check the relationList and value fields. The value field returns a number that indicates the number of topics or groups in the `relationList` field that require optimization.
>
> - When ReportType is commonBuy, check the value of Value. The value is a percentage.
>
> - When ReportType is topic, check the value of Value. The value identifies the Topic that needs to be fixed.
>
> - When ReportType is group, check the value of Value. The value identifies the Group that needs to be fixed.

Success.description: Indicates whether the call was successful.

Code.description: The return code. A value of 200 indicates that the call is successful.

GetRiskList.responseParamsDescription:
> The valid values for the Name and Type fields are:
>
> - topic: A threat is detected in a topic.
>
> - group: A threat is detected in a group.
>
> - offsetCommitTimes: The consumer client commits consumer offsets too frequently.
>
> - multiAssignGroup: The same partition is assigned to multiple consumer threads.
>
> - partitionLeft: The number of partitions is insufficient.
>
> - topicLeft: The number of topics is insufficient.
>
> - diskUsage: The disk usage is high.
>
> - outputIo: The read traffic exceeds the limit.
>
> - inputIo: The write traffic exceeds the limit.
>
> - diskLean: Disk skew exists in the cluster.
>
> - topicLean: A partition skew exists in the topic.
>
> - singlePartitionTopic: A topic with a single partition exists in cloud storage.
>
> - chipProduce: Messages are excessively fragmented.
>
> - syncProduce: The topic uses synchronous sending.
>
> - conversionProduce: The topic format is being converted.
>
> - publicTcpConnection: The number of connections over the internet is excessive.
>
> - tcpConnection: The number of connections is excessive.
>
> - version: The minor version is too low.
>
> - groupLeft: The group quota is insufficient.
>
> - sendTimeGroup: The group has a high consumption latency.
>
> - leaveGroup: A consumer client in the group leaves the queue, which triggers rebalancing.
>
> - rebalanceGroup: The group is undergoing rebalancing.
>
> - saramaClient: A Sarama client is used.
>
> - groupTopicMap: The group subscribes to an excessive number of topics.

The ID of the resource to be tagged. Resource ID rules:

- Instance: instanceId

- Topic: Kafka\_alikafka\_instanceId\_topic

- Group: Kafka\_alikafka\_instanceId\_consumerGroup

For example: If the instance ID is alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx, the Topic name is test-topic, and the Group name is test-consumer-group, the resource IDs are alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx, Kafka\_alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx\_test-topic, and Kafka\_alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx\_test-consumer-group respectively.

> Either the **ResourceId** or **Tag** parameter must be configured to query the tag list bound to resources. Otherwise, the API call fails.
The tag list.

Key.description:
The tag key of the resource.

- If this parameter is empty, all tag keys are matched.

- The tag key can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with aliyun or acs:. It cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

Value.description:
The tag value of the resource.

- If the tag key is empty, this parameter must be empty. If this parameter is empty, all tag values are matched.

- The tag value can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with aliyun or acs:. It cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

NextToken.description: The token for the next query.

TagResource.description: A collection of resources and their tags, including resource ID, resource type, and tag key-value pairs.

- **Instance**

- **Topic**

- **Consumergroup**

ResourceId.description:

- Instance: instanceId

- Topic: Kafka\_alikafka\_instanceId\_topic

- Consumer Group: Kafka\_alikafka\_instanceId\_consumerGroup

For example: If the instance ID is alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx, the Topic name is test-topic, and the Consumer Group name is test-consumer-group, the resource IDs are alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx, Kafka\_alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx\_test-topic, and Kafka\_alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx\_test-consumer-group respectively.

StartInstance.summary: You must purchase and deploy an ApsaraMQ for Kafka instance before you can send and receive messages. This topic describes how to deploy an instance by calling the StartInstance operation.

schema.description: The ID of the instance.
The region ID of the instance.
The ID of the VPC in which the instance is deployed.
The ID of the vSwitch to which the instance is deployed.

The deployment mode of the instance. This parameter is required for provisioned instances. This parameter is not required for Serverless and Confluent instances. Valid values:

- **vpc**: VPC instance

- **eip**: Internet/VPC instance

The deployment mode of the instance must be consistent with the instance type. If the instance is a VPC instance, set this parameter to **vpc**. If the instance is an Internet/VPC instance, set this parameter to **eip**.

The ID of the zone in which the instance is deployed.

- The value must be the zone ID of the vSwitch.

- The value can be in the zoneX or RegionId-X format. For example, you can set the value to zonea or cn-hangzhou-k.

> If resources in the specified zone are insufficient, the instance may be deployed in another zone.

Specifies whether to enable elastic IP addresses (EIPs). Valid values:

- **true**: The instance is an Internet/VPC instance.

- **false**: The instance is a VPC instance.

The value of this parameter must be consistent with the instance type. For example, if the instance is a VPC instance, you must set this parameter to **false**.

Specifies whether to set a new username and password. Valid values:

- **true**: Set a new username and password.

- **false**: Do not set a new username and password.

This parameter is supported only for Internet/VPC instances.

The username.

- For provisioned and Serverless instances, this parameter is supported only for Internet/VPC instances.

- For Confluent instances, you can set this parameter only to root or leave it empty.

Default value: For provisioned and Serverless instances, the default value is username. For Confluent instances, the default value is root.

The password.

- For provisioned and Serverless instances, this parameter is supported only for Internet/VPC instances.

- This parameter is required for Confluent instances. The password must be 8 to 32 characters in length and contain at least three of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Special characters are !@#$%^&\*()\_+-=.

The name of the instance.

This parameter is not supported for Serverless and Confluent instances.

> If you specify this parameter, make sure that the value is unique in the same region.

Specifies whether to deploy the instance across zones.

- true: Deploy the instance across zones.

- false: Do not deploy the instance across zones.

Default value: true.

The security group of the instance.

If you do not specify this parameter, ApsaraMQ for Kafka automatically configures a security group for your instance. If you want to specify this parameter, you must create a security group for the instance in advance. For more information, see [Create a security group](~~25468~~).

The version of the ApsaraMQ for Kafka instance that you want to deploy.

- For provisioned instances, valid values are 2.2.0 and 2.6.2.

- For Serverless instances, the valid value is 3.3.1.

- For Confluent instances, the valid value is 7.4.0.

Default value:

- Provisioned instances: 2.2.0

- Serverless instances: 3.3.1

- Confluent instances: 7.4.0
schema.example:
Reserved Instance Series: 2.2.0
Serverless Instance Series: 3.3.1
Confluent Series: 7.4.0

schema.description:
The initial configurations of the ApsaraMQ for Kafka instance. The value must be a valid JSON string. If you do not specify this parameter, the default value is empty.

> - You cannot specify the Config parameter when you deploy a Confluent instance.
>
> - The enable.acl configuration is not supported for instances of versions earlier than 2.2.0. Only Professional Edition and Serverless instances support access control lists (ACLs).

The following parameters of **Config** are supported for reserved instances:

- **enable.vpc\_sasl\_ssl**

- **enable.acl**

- **kafka.log.retention.hours**

- **kafka.message.max.bytes**

The following parameters of **Config** are supported for Serverless instances:

- **enable.vpc\_sasl\_ssl**

- **enable.acl**

- **log.retention.hours**

- **offsets.retention.minutes**

- **message.max.bytes**

- **auto.create.topics.enable**

- **num.partitions**

<props="china">

For more information, see [UpdateInstanceConfig](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/apsaramq-for-kafka/cloud-message-queue-for-kafka/developer-reference/api-alikafka-2019-09-16-updateinstanceconfig?spm=a2c4g.11186623.0.0.3e9e2a04vLr5nF).

</props>

<props="intl">

For more information, see [UpdateInstanceConfig](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/zh/apsaramq-for-kafka/cloud-message-queue-for-kafka/developer-reference/api-alikafka-2019-09-16-updateinstanceconfig?spm=a2c63.p38356.0.i1).

</props>

The ID of the key that is used for disk encryption in the same region. You can view the key ID in the [Key Management Service (KMS) console](https://kms.console.aliyun.com/?spm=a2c4g.11186623.2.5.336745b8hfiU21) or create a key. For more information, see [Manage keys](~~181610~~).

If you specify this parameter, disk encryption is enabled. You cannot disable disk encryption after it is enabled. When you call this operation, the system checks whether the AliyunServiceRoleForAlikafkaInstanceEncryption service-linked role is created. If the role is not created, the system automatically creates the role. For more information, see [Service-linked Role](~~190460~~).

> - You cannot specify the KMSKeyId parameter when you deploy a Serverless instance.
The alert contact.
The mobile phone number of the alert contact.

A two-dimensional array that consists of the candidate set of the primary zone and the candidate set of the secondary zone. The values can be custom codes (`zone{zone}`) or standard codes (`cn-RegionID-{zone}`).

- If you want to deploy the instance across zones (isCrossZone=true), the candidate set of the primary zone is Zone H or Zone F, and the candidate set of the secondary zone is Zone K, set this parameter to `[[\"zoneh\",\"zonef\"],[\"zonek\"]]`. This example uses custom codes.

  > If you specify multiple zones for the primary or secondary zone, the system selects one of the zones for deployment without a priority. For example, if you set the parameter to `[[\"zoneh\",\"zonef\"],[\"zonek\"]]`, the primary zone of the deployed instance is Zone H or Zone F, and the secondary zone is Zone K.

- If you do not want to deploy the instance across zones (isCrossZone=false) and want to deploy the instance in Zone K, set this parameter to `[[\"zonek\"],[]]`. This example uses a custom code. Note that you must still specify two arrays. The second array, which represents the candidate set of the secondary zone, can be empty \[].

> Relationship between the SelectedZones and VSwitchIds parameters for provisioned instances
>
> - If you specify only VSwitchIds and do not specify SelectedZones, the system preferentially selects the zones that correspond to the vSwitches in VSwitchIds.
Specifies whether to forcibly deploy the instance in the selected zones.

The list of vSwitch IDs. This parameter is required for provisioned and Serverless instances. This parameter is supported for Confluent instances. You must specify at least one of VSwitchIds and VSwitchId. If you specify both, VSwitchIds takes precedence.

TagResources.summary: You can call the TagResources operation to attach tags to resources.

schema.description: The region ID of the resource.

The resource type. Enumeration type. Valid values:

- **INSTANCE**

- **TOPIC**

- **CONSUMERGROUP**

> Case-insensitive.
The list of resource IDs.

items.description:
The ID of the resource to be tagged. Resource ID rules:

- Instance: instanceId

- Topic: Kafka\_alikafka\_instanceId\_topic

- Group: Kafka\_alikafka\_instanceId\_consumerGroup

For example: If the instance ID is alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx, the Topic name is test-topic, and the Group name is test-consumer-group, then the respective resource IDs are alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx, Kafka\_alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx\_test-topic, and Kafka\_alikafka\_post-cn-v0h1fgs2xxxx\_test-consumer-group.

schema.description: The list of tags.

Value.description:

- Can be empty.

- Supports up to 128 characters, cannot start with aliyun or acs:, and cannot contain http\:// or https\://.

UpdateConsumerOffset.title: UpdateConsumerOffset
UpdateConsumerOffset.summary: The UpdateConsumerOffset operation resets the consumer offset of a consumer group.
UpdateConsumerOffset.description:
This operation resets the consumer offset of a specified consumer group. You can reset the consumer offset by timestamp or by a specific offset value. Using different parameter combinations, you can perform the following tasks:

- Consume messages from the latest offset by setting the consumer offset to the latest position. This is supported for a single topic or all topics.

- Consume messages from the offset of a specified time point by providing a timestamp. This is supported for a single topic or all topics.

- Reset the consumer offset for a specific partition by providing the target partition ID and consumer offset. This is supported only for a single topic.
UpdateConsumerOffset.requestParamsDescription:
(1) Reset the consumer offset of all subscribed topics for a consumer group to the latest consumer offset. To do this, set the Time parameter to a value less than 0. We recommend that you set the value to -1.

```
{
  "RegionId":"cn-beijing",
  "InstanceId":"alikafka_post-cn-xxxxxx",
  "Topic":"",
  "ConsumerId":"ConsumerGroup1",
  "ResetType": timestamp,
  "Time":-1,
  "Offsets": null
}
```

(2) Reset the consumer offset of all subscribed topics for a consumer group based on the Time parameter. The Time parameter specifies the time in the Unix timestamp format in milliseconds.

```
{
  "RegionId":"cn-beijing",
  "InstanceId":"alikafka_post-cn-xxxxxx",
  "Topic":"",
  "ConsumerId":"ConsumerGroup1",
  "ResetType": timestamp,
  "Time":1679587200000,
  "Offsets": null
}
```

(3) Reset the consumer offset of a specific topic for a consumer group to the latest consumer offset. To do this, set the Time parameter to a value less than 0. We recommend that you set the value to -1.

```
{
  "RegionId":"cn-beijing",
  "InstanceId":"alikafka_post-cn-xxxxxx",
  "Topic":"topic1",
  "ConsumerId":"ConsumerGroup1",
  "ResetType": timestamp,
  "Time":-1,
  "Offsets": null
}
```

(4) Reset the consumer offset of a specific topic for a consumer group based on the Time parameter. The Time parameter specifies the time in the Unix timestamp format in milliseconds.

```
{
  "RegionId":"cn-beijing",
  "InstanceId":"alikafka_post-cn-xxxxxxx",
  "Topic":"topic1",
  "ConsumerId":"ConsumerG1",
  "ResetType": timestamp,
  "Time":1679587200000,
  "Offsets": null
}
```

(5) Reset the consumer offset of a specific topic for a consumer group based on the provided offsets.

UpdateInstanceConfig.title: UpdateInstanceConfig
UpdateInstanceConfig.summary: After an instance is deployed, you can modify configurations such as enabling Access Control List (ACL) and SSL, the message retention period, and the maximum message size. This topic describes how to call the UpdateInstanceConfig operation to modify the configuration of an instance.
UpdateInstanceConfig.description:
## **Permission information**

RAM users must obtain authorization before they can call the **UpdateInstanceConfig** operation. For more information, see [RAM access policies](~~185815~~).

| API                  | Action                   | Resource                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| UpdateInstanceConfig | alikafka: UpdateInstance | acs:alikafka:*:*:{instanceId} |
UpdateInstanceConfig.requestParamsDescription:
### Description of the Config parameter

| Name                      | Type   | Value range                                                                      | Default value | Description                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| enable.vpc\_sasl\_ssl     | String | `"true"`: Enable. `"false"`: Do not enable.                                      | `"false"`     | Whether to enable VPC transmission encryption. If you want to enable it, you must also enable ACL.                                                       |
| enable.acl                | String | `"true"`: Enable. `"false"`: Do not enable.                                      | `"false"`     | Whether to enable ACL. Instance versions below 2.2.0 are not supported. Only Professional Edition and Serverless Edition instances support enabling ACL. |
| kafka.log.retention.hours | String | Currently only supports selecting integers within the \[24,480] range.           | `"72"`        | Message retention period (hours).                                                                                                                        |
| kafka.message.max.bytes   | String | Currently only supports selecting integers within the \[1048576,10485760] range. | `"1048576"`   | Maximum message size (bytes).                                                                                                                            |
| log.retention.hours       | String | Currently only supports selecting integers within the \[24,8760] range.          | `"72"`        | Message retention period (hours). Only supports serverless instances.                                                                                    |
| offsets.retention.minutes | String | Currently only supports selecting integers within the \[1440,43200] range.       | `"10080"`     | Consumer offset retention period (minutes). Only supports serverless instances.                                                                          |
| message.max.bytes         | String | Currently only supports selecting integers within the \[1048576,10485760] range. | `"1048576"`   | Maximum message size (bytes). Only supports serverless instances.                                                                                        |
| auto.create.topics.enable | String | `"true"`: Enable. `"false"`: Do not enable.                                      | `"false"`     | Enable or disable automatic topic creation. Only supports serverless instances.                                                                          |
| num.partitions            | String | Currently only supports selecting integers within the \[1,800] range.            | `"3"`         | Number of partitions for automatically created topics. Only supports serverless instances.                                                               |

UpdateTopicConfig.summary: After a topic is created, you can modify its configurations, such as the message retention period and maximum message size. This topic describes how to call this API operation to modify topic configurations.

schema.description: The region ID of the instance.
The instance ID.
The topic name.

The key of the topic configuration.

- You can modify the configurations only for topics that use the local storage engine on reserved instances. You cannot modify the configurations for topics that use the cloud storage engine.

- You can modify the configurations of topics for Serverless instances.

- For `local topics` on reserved instances, the supported keys are \`retention.ms\`, \`max.message.bytes\`, \`message.timestamp.type\`, and \`message.timestamp.difference.max.ms\`.

- For Serverless instances, the supported keys are \`retention.hours\`, \`max.message.bytes\`, \`message.timestamp.type\`, and \`message.timestamp.difference.max.ms\`.

The value of the topic configuration.

- The following configurations are supported for Serverless instances:

  - `retention.hours` specifies the message retention period. The value must be a string. The value must be in the range of 24 to 8,760.

  - `max.message.bytes` specifies the maximum message size. The value must be a string. The value must be in the range of 1,048,576 to 10,485,760.

  - `message.timestamp.type` specifies the message timestamp type. \`CreateTime\` indicates the timestamp that is specified by the producer when the message is sent. If no timestamp is specified, the time when the message is created on the client is used. \`LogAppendTime\` indicates the time when the message is stored on the server. Valid values: \`CreateTime\` and \`LogAppendTime\`.

  - `message.timestamp.difference.max.ms` specifies the maximum allowed difference between the timestamp of the server that receives the message and the timestamp specified in the message. If \`message.timestamp.type\` is set to \`CreateTime\` and the time difference exceeds this threshold, **the message is rejected**. This configuration does not take effect if \`message.timestamp.type\` is set to \`LogAppendTime\`.

- The following configurations are supported for reserved instances:

  - `retention.ms` specifies the message retention period. The value must be a string. The value must be in the range of 3,600,000 to 31,536,000,000.

  - `max.message.bytes` specifies the maximum message size. The value must be a string. The value must be in the range of 1,048,576 to 10,485,760.

  - `message.timestamp.type` specifies the message timestamp type. \`CreateTime\` indicates the timestamp that is specified by the producer when the message is sent. If no timestamp is specified, the time when the message is created on the client is used. \`LogAppendTime\` indicates the time when the message is stored on the server. Valid values: \`CreateTime\` and \`LogAppendTime\`.

  - `message.timestamp.difference.max.ms` specifies the maximum allowed difference between the timestamp of the server that receives the message and the timestamp specified in the message. If \`message.timestamp.type\` is set to \`CreateTime\` and the time difference exceeds this threshold, **the message is rejected**. This configuration does not take effect if \`message.timestamp.type\` is set to \`LogAppendTime\`.

UpgradeInstanceVersion.title: UpgradeInstanceVersion
UpgradeInstanceVersion.summary: Upgrades the version of an instance.
UpgradeInstanceVersion.description:
## **Permission description**

RAM users must be authorized before they can call the **UpgradeInstanceVersion** API. For more information about authorization, see [RAM access policy](~~185815~~).

| API                    | Action         | Resource                      |
| ---------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------- |
| UpgradeInstanceVersion | UpdateInstance | acs:alikafka:*:*:{instanceId} |

## **QPS limits**

The request frequency is limited to 2 queries per second (QPS) for a single user.
UpgradeInstanceVersion.requestParamsDescription:
## **Description of the TargetVersion parameter**

| Open source version before upgrade | Minor version before upgrade | Target open source version | Open source version after upgrade | Minor version after upgrade |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| 0.10.2                             | Not the latest minor version | 0.10.2                     | 0.10.2                            | Latest minor version        |
| 0.10.2                             | Not the latest minor version | 2.2.0                      | 2.2.0                             | Latest minor version        |
| 0.10.2                             | Latest minor version         | 2.2.0                      | 2.2.0                             | Latest minor version        |
| 2.2.0                              | Not the latest minor version | 2.2.0                      | 2.2.0                             | Latest minor version        |

For more information about minor version updates, see [Upgrade instance version](~~113173~~).

schema.description: The instance ID.

The disk capacity. Unit: GB.

- The disk capacity must be greater than or equal to the current disk capacity of the instance.

- For more information about the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If the instance is a Serverless instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.
The region ID of the instance.

The traffic specification. This parameter is recommended.

- The traffic specification must be greater than or equal to the current traffic specification of the instance.

- You must specify only one of the IoMax and IoMaxSpec parameters. If you specify both, the value of the IoMaxSpec parameter takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only the IoMaxSpec parameter.

- For more information about the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If the instance is a Serverless instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.

The peak traffic. This parameter is not recommended.

- The peak traffic must be greater than or equal to the current peak traffic of the instance.

- You must specify only one of the IoMax and IoMaxSpec parameters. If you specify both, the value of the IoMaxSpec parameter takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only the IoMaxSpec parameter.

- For more information about the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If the instance is a Serverless instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.

The edition of the instance.

If the instance uses the pay-as-you-go billing method (PaidType=1), valid values are:

- normal: Standard Edition (High-write)

- professional: Professional Edition (High-write)

- professionalForHighRead: Professional Edition (High-read)

If the instance uses the pay-as-you-go billing method for reserved capacity and the Serverless billing method for elastic scaling (PaidType=3), valid values are:

- normal: Serverless Standard Edition

For more information, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The number of partitions. This parameter is recommended.

- You must specify only one of the PartitionNum and TopicQuota parameters. We recommend that you specify only the PartitionNum parameter.

- If you specify both parameters, the system verifies whether the values of the two parameters are equivalent based on the topic-based sales model. If the values are not equivalent, the system returns a failure response. If the values are equivalent, the purchase is made based on the value of the PartitionNum parameter.

- For more information about the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If the instance is a Serverless instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.

The number of topics. This parameter is not recommended.

- You must specify only one of the PartitionNum and TopicQuota parameters. We recommend that you specify only the PartitionNum parameter.

- If you specify both parameters, the system verifies whether the values of the two parameters are equivalent based on the topic-based sales model. If the values are not equivalent, the system returns a failure response. If the values are equivalent, the purchase is made based on the value of the PartitionNum parameter.

- The default value of this parameter varies based on the traffic specification. If you specify a value that is greater than the default value, you are charged for the extra topics.

- For more information about the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> If the instance is a Serverless instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.

Specifies whether to enable Internet access for the instance. Valid values:

- true: enables Internet access.

- false: disables Internet access.

The Internet traffic.

- The Internet traffic must be greater than or equal to the current Internet traffic of the instance.

- For more information about the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> * If you set **EipModel** to **true**, you must set **EipMax** to a value that is greater than 0.
>
> * If you set **EipModel** to **false**, you must set **EipMax** to **0**.
>
> * If the instance is a Serverless instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.
The settings for the Serverless instance. This parameter is required when you upgrade a Serverless instance.

ReservedPublishCapacity.description:
The reserved capacity for publishing messages. You can specify only an integer. The minimum value is 60. This parameter is required for Serverless instances.

> The actual upper limit is subject to the inventory in the current region. For more information, see the instance purchase page.

ReservedSubscribeCapacity.description:
The reserved capacity for subscribing to messages. You can specify only an integer. The minimum value is 20. This parameter is required for Serverless instances.

> The actual upper limit is subject to the inventory in the current region. For more information, see the instance purchase page.

UpgradePostPayOrder.title: UpgradePostPayOrder
UpgradePostPayOrder.description: Before you call this operation, make sure that you fully understand the billing methods and pricing of pay-as-you-go instances. For more information, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

schema.description: The instance ID.

The disk capacity.

- The specified disk capacity must be greater than or equal to the current disk capacity of the instance.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> This parameter is not required when you upgrade a Confluent series instance.
The region ID of the instance.

The traffic peak (not recommended).

- The specified traffic peak must be greater than or equal to the current traffic peak of the instance.

- You must specify either the traffic peak or the traffic specification. If both parameters are specified, the traffic specification takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only the traffic specification.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The specification type.

Valid values for Kafka instances:

- **normal**: Standard Edition (high write)

- **professional**: Professional Edition (high write)

- **professionalForHighRead**: Professional Edition (high read)

Valid values for Confluent instances:

- **professional**: Professional Edition

- **enterprise**: Enterprise Edition

You cannot downgrade an instance from Professional Edition to Standard Edition. For more information about these specification types, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The number of partitions (recommended).

- You must specify either the number of partitions or the topic specification. We recommend that you specify only the number of partitions.

- If both the number of partitions and the topic specification are specified, the system verifies whether they are equivalent based on the old topic sales model. If they are not equivalent, the operation fails. If they are equivalent, the system purchases the instance based on the number of partitions.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

The number of topics (not recommended).

- You must specify either the number of partitions or the topic specification. We recommend that you specify only the number of partitions.

- If both the number of partitions and the topic specification are specified, the system verifies whether they are equivalent based on the old topic sales model. If they are not equivalent, the operation fails. If they are equivalent, the system purchases the instance based on the number of partitions.

- The default value varies based on the traffic specification. Additional fees are charged if the value exceeds the default value.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

Specifies whether to enable Internet access. Valid values:

- true: enables Internet access

- false: disables Internet access

The Internet traffic.

- The specified Internet traffic must be greater than or equal to the current Internet traffic of the instance.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).

> * If **EipModel** is set to **true**, **EipMax** must be greater than 0.
>
> * If **EipModel** is set to **false**, **EipMax** must be set to **0**.

The traffic specification (recommended).

- The specified traffic specification must be greater than or equal to the current traffic specification of the instance.

- You must specify either the traffic peak or the traffic specification. If both parameters are specified, the traffic specification takes precedence. We recommend that you specify only the traffic specification.

- For the valid values, see [Billing](~~84737~~).
